title: gateway: make 429 rate-limit error payload consistent + machine-readable for SDK retries
author: Amara Diallo
release_notes: Gateway now returns a consistent JSON error payload for HTTP 429 across routes, including stable machine-readable fields (error.code, rate_limit.*) to support SDK retry classifiers. No changes to status codes; message text remains best-effort and may vary by route.
commits: gateway/errors: introduce shared RateLimitErrorPayload builder + tests
gateway/middleware: normalize 429 responses from upstreams (quota + burst limiter)
gateway/headers: ensure Retry-After is set when reset info is available (mirrors payload)
docs/internal: add examples + contract notes for SDKs
body:
Title: gateway: make 429 rate-limit error payload consistent + machine-readable for SDK retries

Context
SDK parity work (ENG-2482) needs a reliable way to classify rate-limit responses across endpoints and environments. Today we return HTTP 429 consistently, but the JSON body shape varies by route and by limiter source (burst limiter vs. quota). This is contributing to retry misclassification (notably TS being too aggressive because it can’t reliably tell whether a 429 is "retry soon" vs "hard quota"). See SUP-9334.

What this PR changes
- Introduces a shared builder for rate-limit error payloads and uses it across all public Hosted API routes.
- Normalizes 429s emitted from multiple sources (local limiter, upstream service quota, legacy exceptions) into a single JSON shape.
- Adds stable, machine-readable fields for SDKs:
  - error.code: always "rate_limit_exceeded" for 429
  - error.type: always "rate_limit_error" for 429
  - rate_limit.scope: "api_key" | "project" | "org" (when known)
  - rate_limit.limit: integer (when known)
  - rate_limit.remaining: integer (when known)
  - rate_limit.reset_at: RFC3339 timestamp (when known)
  - rate_limit.retry_after_ms: integer (when known)
- Ensures the payload is consistent even when we don’t know all fields: unknown fields are omitted (not null), and error.code/type are always present.
- Keeps human-readable message best-effort; SDKs should key off error.code/type + rate_limit.retry_after_ms.

Example response (new)
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Retry-After: 2
x-request-id: req_01HRQ7KJ0C0P7Z8J7G9B5R2M4V
content-type: application/json

{
  "error": {
    "type": "rate_limit_error",
    "code": "rate_limit_exceeded",
    "message": "Rate limit exceeded. Please retry after 2000ms.",
    "request_id": "req_01HRQ7KJ0C0P7Z8J7G9B5R2M4V"
  },
  "rate_limit": {
    "scope": "api_key",
    "limit": 60,
    "remaining": 0,
    "retry_after_ms": 2000,
    "reset_at": "2025-02-07T19:22:10Z"
  }
}

Notes / non-goals
- Non-goal: changing rate-limit policy or thresholds.
- Non-goal: introducing server-side retries.
- We do not guarantee message string stability; only error.code/type + rate_limit fields are intended as contract.
- If reset time is not available, we still return 429 with error.code/type, and omit rate_limit.reset_at + retry_after_ms.

Why this helps SDKs
- Retry classifiers can now consistently check error.code == "rate_limit_exceeded".
- When present, rate_limit.retry_after_ms can be used to cap exponential backoff and respect gateway guidance.
- SDKs can distinguish between "burst" and "quota" sources via scope (when we can infer it), which helps avoid long retry storms on hard quota.

Testing
- Added route-level contract tests verifying exact response shape for 429 across: /chat/completions, /completions, /embeddings, /rerank.
- Added unit tests for payload builder behavior (field omission, header vs payload consistency).
- Verified that response headers remain unchanged except for stricter Retry-After emission when reset info exists.

Rollout
- Safe to roll out behind standard deployment; no client changes required.
- After deploy, DevEx will update SDK retry spec to reference error.code/type + rate_limit.retry_after_ms as the canonical signal.

Checklist
- [x] Contract tests added for all public routes
- [x] Does not log secrets; does not include auth context in payload
- [x] Error payload includes request_id (also in x-request-id header)
- [x] Reviewed with SRE for retry-safety implications

Review conversation (highlights)
- Brian Murphy: "Can we commit to a stable field name for retry guidance? SDKs need a single knob." Author: "Added rate_limit.retry_after_ms and made it the preferred field; headers still include Retry-After when we can compute it. Documented in docs/internal/api/errors.md."
- Rafael Mendes: "Please ensure we never set Retry-After to 0 for burst flaps; that can amplify storms." Author: "Clamped to minimum 50ms when computed, and omitted entirely when unknown. Added tests covering clamp behavior."
- Ethan Park: "Do we risk breaking existing customers parsing legacy payloads?" Author: "Status code + existing error.message remain; payload shape is additive from a contract perspective, but some routes previously returned different top-level keys. We’ve kept the legacy keys for one release cycle on the two legacy routes and added a TODO + metric to track clients still receiving legacy fields."

CI
All checks passing. Contract tests added to reduce regression risk for SDK conformance harness.

Related
- Companion PR: PR-18342 (clarify response headers like x-request-id / Retry-After) for better SDK integration.
- Project: SDK parity audit + retry standardization (ENG-2482).
